newsitem.title: GERMANY: Dresdner to open direct banking unit in H2 1997.
newsitem.headline: Dresdner to open direct banking unit in H2 1997.

text.p: Dresdner Bank AG plans to launch a direct banking unit in the second half of 1997, the company said in a statement accompaning its nine-month results on Thursday.
"With a new kind of offer, that will stand out from the rest the rest of the market, we want to make optimal use of growing business potential," Dresdner said in a statement.
Dresdner is the last of Germany's large banks to set up a direct banking unit.

Dresdner also said it planned to introduce "a new quality" to its retail banking in 1997 and would increase use of technology in dealings with customers, using the resources thus freed up to offer more focused advisory services.
Strict cost management would be imposed in the domestic branch network, with an unspecified number of branches to be closed down, Dresdner said.
"We have set ourselves the goal of reducing our cost/earnings ratio to clearly below 70 percent in the medium term," the statement quoted Dresdner chief executive Juergen Sarrazin as saying.
